name: wy60
why: A terminal emulator for a vintage Wyse 60 terminal, a window into old-school hardware behaviour and escape codes.

brief.what_it_is: wy60 is a terminal emulator that aims to behave like a Wyse 60 compatible terminal, the vintage ASCII terminal from the early 1980s. The only description available is the Brew formula line: 'Wyse 60 compatible terminal emulator', with an executable named wy60. The archived Google Code homepage did not render any project content, so I could not confirm what input it accepts (a serial line, a network connection, or a host session) or what it displays beyond the general idea of emulating Wyse 60 escape codes.
brief.why_it_exists: Not stated in anything I could read. The scout note suggests it is a window into old-school hardware behaviour and escape codes, but that is the scout's framing, not the author's.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond the Homebrew formula was visible. The Brew metadata names a single executable, wy60, and has no caveats. I did not see build steps, runtime requirements, or configuration.
brief.standout: The Wyse 60 is a specific, historically significant video terminal, so a faithful emulator of it is a niche and nostalgic tool. The scout note calls it a window into hardware-era escape codes, which is a reasonable angle, but I could not verify any specific cleverness from the source.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage is a Google Code Archive page, meaning the project was moved to read-only long-term storage when Google Code shut down in 2015. The archive page showed no release dates or commit history, and the wiki URL returned the same empty shell.
brief.caveats: The homepage was effectively unreachable for content: it returned only the Google Code Archive shell and states that JavaScript is required. The wiki page gave the same result. Because of this, the brief has no README text, no commands, no quotes, and no verified feature list. Anyone writing the entry should check the upstream source or a mirror before making claims about features, platform support, or licensing.
